title: Koalas Sleep to Survive Daily Poison
description: Discover the shocking evolutionary reason why koalas sleep for 22 hours a day—it is a brutal fight for survival against toxic leaves.
instagram_caption: Think koalas are just lazy? 🐨 Think again. That cute sleep is actually a daily battle to process lethal poison. Discover the extreme evolutionary trade-off behind their 22-hour nap cycle! #animals #wildlife #nature #koala #science

segments.narration: A koala asleep in a tree isn't just resting. It is locked in a silent, desperate battle to survive a dose of daily poison.

koala nose close up breathing slowly

segments.narration: But neutralizing these toxic eucalyptus leaves requires massive energy, from a food source that offers virtually zero calories in return.
broll_queries: koala reaching for eucalyptus leaf forest

segments.narration: To prevent starvation, the koala makes a drastic trade-off: shutting down its body and brain to conserve every drop of energy.
broll_queries: koala head tucked in fur sleeping

segments.narration: This twenty-two-hour sleep cycle is actually an evolutionary masterstroke, turning a toxic wasteland into an exclusive home.
